title: Priority lift and decommitment protocol for key accounts
creator: Emily Chen
description: Problem: High-touch accounts occasionally request urgent roadmap changes or feature accelerations. Engineering and Product teams have historically accepted these ad hoc, causing unpredictable scope creep, SLA strain, and missed OKRs. We need a lightweight, enforceable protocol to temporarily elevate ("priority lift") a customer ask, capture commitments, and then decommit or normalize the request at a defined cadence.
proposal:
Introduce a Priority Lift + Decommitment Protocol (PLDP) that standardizes how top accounts get temporary prioritization. Key elements:

1) Trigger conditions: clear signals that justify a lift (contract renewal at risk, legal requirement, strategic partner launch, material revenue impact > $X/month).
2) Timebox and scope: lifts are approved for a fixed window (default 4 weeks) with a scoped acceptance criteria and one of three outcomes at window close: Adopt (add to roadmap), Defer (remove and re-evaluate), or Ship-as-partial (deliver a scoped shim).
3) Decision arbiter: a small panel (PM, Eng lead, Customer Success AE) that records rationale and acceptance criteria in the ticket.
4) Commitment ledger: PLDP entries create a short record in the customer intake ledger tracked in Confluence with links to dashboards for latency/cost impact.
5) Decommitment choreography: automated reminders at T-7 and T-2 days before window close, plus a canary rollout requirement for any code changes under lift.

The protocol ties to existing roadmap lanes and provides a financial/backstop policy for cases where decommitment causes churn risk.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A standardized PLDP request form exists in the intake UI and is used for all top-account escalation tickets.
2) Decision arbiter panel process documented with template rationale.
3) Engineering capacity impact (tokens/throughput cost and SLA delta) is estimated within 2 business days for any approved lift.
4) Three pilot lifts completed with full decommitment or adoption flow, and retrospective notes.
4) Dashboard shows active lifts and expected cost delta per week.
metrics:
- # of active priority lifts
- Mean time from lift approval to decision (target < 30 days)
- % of lifts that result in permanent roadmap adoption
- Delta in avg P95 latency and per-token cost during lifts
- Churn incidents tied to decommitments (target: zero major churnes)
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Weeks 1-3): Design PLDP intake form + decision template; align CS and Sales on trigger signals.
Phase 2 (Weeks 4-6): Implement Confluence ledger + intake form; hooks to Linear to auto-create PLDP tickets; add two reminder automations for T-7/T-2.
Phase 3 (Weeks 7-12): Run 3 pilot lifts with Engineering and CS; collect metrics and retro; adjust default timebox.
Phase 4 (Post-pilot): Bake into Customer SLA docs, surface active lifts in Console as 'priority overlays' for affected customers.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Engineering bandwidth consumed by repeated lifts. Mitigation: hard caps per quarter and requirement to provide measurable customer ROI for each lift.
Risk: Ambiguity in scope leads to surprise work. Mitigation: require acceptance criteria and a signed PM/CS/Eng acknowledgment before approval.
Risk: Reputational churn when a lift is decommitted. Mitigation: decommitment playbook includes customer comms template and optional discount/credit path approved by Rev Ops.
notes:
- This is intentionally lightweight compared with full change control to keep top accounts engaged without derailing OKRs.
- Coordinate with Legal on any lift that touches contractual SLAs.
- Consider mapping lifts to a finite 'priority budget' per customer each fiscal year.
